title: The Wolf of Wall Street
tagline: Money talks and bullshit takes the bus.
about: A Long Island penny-stock broker builds Stratton Oakmont into a machine for money, drugs and excess, with the FBI one step behind.

Poached king prawns, Marie Rose, iceberg.How to make it16 raw king prawns, peeled with tails on125g whole-egg mayonnaise2 tbsp tomato sauce1 tsp Worcestershire sauce1 tsp hot sauce1 lemon1/2 iceberg lettuce, finely shredded1 avocado, diced1/4 tsp sweet paprikaDrop the prawns into simmering salted water for 2 minutes until just pink, then into iced water.Stir the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, Worcestershire, hot sauce and a squeeze of lemon into Marie Rose sauce.Fill 4 chilled glasses with lettuce and avocado.Hang the prawns over the rim, spoon over the sauce and dust with paprika.Aunt Emma's smoked salmon blini with caviarAunt Emma holds the Swiss money. Buckwheat blini, smoked salmon, creme fraiche, caviar.How to make it100g buckwheat flour50g plain flour1 tsp baking powder200ml milk1 egg30g butter, melted200g smoked salmon150g creme fraiche50g salmon roe or caviar1 small bunch dill1 lemonWhisk the flours, baking powder and a pinch of salt with the milk, egg and half the butter.Brush a frying pan with butter and cook tablespoons of batter until bubbles show, then flip.Top each blini with creme fraiche and a curl of salmon.Finish with a little caviar, dill and a squeeze of lemon.Owner's tableNaomi's lobster thermidor with shoestring friesJordan throws lobsters at the FBI. Lobster in mustard cream, gruyere crust, fries.How to make it2 cooked lobsters, halved lengthways50g butter1 French shallot, finely chopped1 tbsp plain flour200ml milk100ml thickened cream2 tsp Dijon mustard1 tbsp tarragon, chopped80g gruyere, grated750g frozen shoestring fries1 lemon, in wedgesBake the fries at 220°C until crisp while you make the sauce.Pull the lobster meat from the shells and tails, cut into chunks and keep the shells.Soften the shallot in the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk and cream and simmer until thick.Stir in the mustard, tarragon, half the cheese and the lobster, then pile back into the shells.Scatter with the rest of the cheese and grill until bubbling and golden, then serve with the fries and lemon.Steve Madden IPO steak au poivre with fritesSteve Madden goes public. Peppered eye fillet, cognac cream, frites.How to make it4 x 200g eye fillet steaks2 tbsp black peppercorns, coarsely cracked1 tbsp olive oil40g butter60ml cognac150ml beef stock150ml thickened cream750g frozen thick-cut chips1 bunch watercressBake the chips at 220°C until golden.Press the pepper into both sides of the steaks and season with salt.Sear in the oil and butter over high heat, 3 to 4 minutes a side for medium rare, then rest.Pour the cognac into the pan and let it bubble off, then add the stock and cream and boil until it coats a spoon.Serve the steaks with the sauce, frites and watercress.PlatedLemmon 714 lemon meringue tartJordan calls the Lemmons the holy grail. Sharp lemon curd, scorched meringue.How to make it1 23cm sweet shortcrust tart case, blind baked4 lemons, zested and juiced200g caster sugar, plus 150g for the meringue4 eggs, separated, plus 2 yolks150g butter, cubed2 tbsp cornflour1/2 tsp cream of tartarWhisk the lemon zest and juice, 200g sugar, 6 yolks and cornflour in a pan over low heat until thick.Take off the heat, whisk in the butter, pour into the tart case and chill until set.Whisk the whites with the cream of tartar to soft peaks, then add the rest of the sugar a spoon at a time until glossy.Pile the meringue over the curd and bake at 200°C until golden at the tips.Cool for 10 minutes before slicing.LoggedMark Hanna's Absolut martini, straight upTwo more every five minutes. Absolut vodka, dry vermouth, lemon twist.How to make it300ml Absolut vodka40ml dry vermouth1 lemon2 cups ice cubesStir the vodka and vermouth with ice in a jug for 30 seconds until very cold.Strain into 4 chilled martini glasses and twist a strip of lemon peel over each.An ice-cold non-alcoholic beerNo alcohol. That's the point.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
